answers.answered_by: Answered by: Gemini (gemini-3.5-flash-lite), function calling · 3 model calls
answers.answer_text:

Answered by: Gemini (gemini-3.5-flash-lite), function calling · 3 model calls

Scope: get_satisfaction_vs_revenue: all loaded data | get_data_coverage: all loaded data.

Findings

The overall correlation between satisfaction and store-year revenue is +0.235 across 100 store-years.
In Market tier 1-Small, the correlation is -0.009 with a mean satisfaction of 3.54 and mean store-year revenue of $72,964.67 (30 store-years).
In Market tier 2-Minor, the correlation is -0.088 with a mean satisfaction of 3.06 and mean store-year revenue of $96,821 (30 store-years).
In Market tier 3-Medium, the correlation is -0.009 with a mean satisfaction of 3.12 and mean store-year revenue of $145,690 (25 store-years).
In Market tier 4-Large, the correlation is +0.181 with a mean satisfaction of 4.28 and mean store-year revenue of $414,649.33 (15 store-years).
5 Website store-years were excluded because they lack in-store surveys.

Interpretation

Association is not causation, so correlation cannot show that satisfaction causes revenue.
Market tier confounds the comparison because larger stores earn more regardless of satisfaction.
Within Market tiers, the correlation is near zero or weak.
Revenue is not profit because costs are not in the data.
The survey reflects active customers only and excludes those who stopped shopping.
